A grievance, appeal or exception gives you the chance to tell us what’s on your mind so we can work to find a solution. All members with Medicare, Medicaid and prescription drug coverage have the right to file these requests. Here’s some information to help you get started with your grievance, appeal or exception. Grievances, appeals and exceptions explained Grievance —A grievance is a complaint about any aspect of your Medicare plan. For example, if you received poor service or you think our plan notices are hard to understand. Appeal —An appeal, or redetermination, is a request for us to reconsider an initial decision you disagree with. Examples include a denial of payment or coverage for a service. Exceptions —Exceptions are a type of coverage determination for prescriptions drugs. These requests may include covering drugs not currently on Humana’s Drug List or waiving certain limits. Who can submit grievances, appeals and exceptions Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) —You (member), a person you appoint or your physician. Medicare Part D (Prescription drug coverage) —You (member), a person you appoint, your prescribing doctor or other prescriber. How to submit grievances, appeals and exceptions Online File an appeal or grievance online Mail or fax Download a form, fill it out and send it to the address or fax number on the form: Appeal, Complaint or Grievance Form – English pdf opens in new window Appeal, Complaint or Grievance Form – Spanish pdf opens in new window Request for Redetermination of Medicare Prescription Drug Denial Form – English pdf opens in new window Request for Redetermination of Medicare Prescription Drug Denial Form – Spanish pdf opens in new window Note: Be sure to submit any required supporting documents (receipts, medical records or a letter from your doctor) with your form. Phone To file an oral grievance, appeal or exception, call the Customer Care number on the back of your Humana member ID card. You can also get help with any questions or problems you have filling out the form, or check the status on a previously filed appeal. ## Findings

I searched Humana's public "Medical and Pharmacy Coverage Policies" library (mcp.humana.com), Humana's commercial and Medicare Advantage prior‑authorization lists, and Humana's provider manual. Here is what I could and could not confirm.

**What exists publicly:** Humana does publish a policy titled **"Shoulder Arthroplasty"** on its Medical and Pharmacy Coverage Policies site — but as currently listed there, it is explicitly labeled **"Shoulder Arthroplasty – Medicare Advantage"** (most recent entries show an effective date of 8/3/2026, reviewed 7/14/2026). Humana's own "Understanding the Process" page states these coverage policies are developed specifically to fill gaps in **Medicare Advantage** coverage guidance — they are not represented as commercial/ACA policy documents.

**Quinn's plan is Commercial/ACA**, not Medicare Advantage. I could not locate a Medicare-Advantage-labeled policy that Humana states also governs commercial members, and I could not find any separate, publicly posted "Shoulder Arthroplasty" medical-necessity policy for Humana commercial plans on Humana's own sites.

What I *could* confirm about the commercial pathway: Humana's **Commercial Preauthorization and Notification List** (effective 7/1/2024, revised 12/10/2024) lists CPT 23472 under "Orthopedic surgeries: hip, knee and shoulder arthroplasty," which requires prior authorization and states that this category is **"Managed by Cohere Health nationally"** (Cohere is a delegated utilization-management vendor). Separately, Humana's 2025 Provider Manual states that "Humana's Medicare coverage policies, MCG care guidelines, and ASAM guidelines are available to practitioners and members at Humana.com" — implying MCG (Milliman Care Guidelines), a licensed/proprietary clinical-criteria product, is a source used in review. Neither Cohere's specific shoulder-arthroplasty criteria nor the MCG "Shoulder Arthroplasty" guideline is published in full text on a free public Humana or Cohere webpage — both are gated/licensed content.

Because of this, I cannot honestly point to one specific, publicly retrievable document as "the" governing medical policy applied to Quinn's commercial denial — the only full-text "Shoulder Arthroplasty" policy Humana publishes is designated for Medicare Advantage, not commercial members.
